audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1], whys[4] and `mid` describe the level-6 spike as a resistance drain only, and `late` describes Zac's late game with no mention of the mechanic that decides whether a kill is a kill.
audit.why: Subjugate takes 40% of current armour and MR and 20/25/30% of the target's maximum health as damage, healing Trundle for the same amount and doubling over the next 4 seconds. Against the health bar Zac builds, the max-health half is the bigger half. And Cell Division is a revive on a FIVE-MINUTE cooldown: on fatal damage he splits into four bloblets, each carrying a share of his maximum health, armour and magic resist, and he comes back on whatever survives. Killing the bloblets is the kill, and once he has spent it you own five minutes against a mortal Zac — a spike the page never mentions in either direction.
audit.corrected: Subjugate: 40% of resists plus a fifth of max health, healing the same. Cell Division: a four-bloblet revive on a 5-minute cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fields give Pillar of Ice a knock-up: spikes[3] "Pillar of Ice placed in his landing zone knocks him up", wants.you[2] "to knock him up and cancel the engage", whys[2] "ends with a knock-up into your domain".
audit.why: Pillar of Ice creates impassable terrain and slows nearby enemies — there is no displacement in it. That matters more here than in most matchups because the correct play against Elastic Slingshot is a placement, not a reaction: the pillar has to sit ACROSS the flight path, where it is terrain the launch collides with, rather than on the landing spot waiting to knock him out of the air. A player told to expect a knock-up will place it in the wrong location and then blame his timing.
audit.corrected: Pillar of Ice is terrain plus a slow. Lay it across the Slingshot's flight path, not on the landing point.
sources: audits/top/zac__trundle.json (mirror, point 4 — pillar cutting the slingshot angle confirmed)

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0], `early`, spikes[2] and `mid` all describe Chomp's debuff as an "attack-speed steal" or "AS debuff", and build the trading plan on it. Unstable Matter is never named; `early` instead refers to "his W slow".
audit.why: Chomp saps Attack Damage and slows movement — no attack-speed component anywhere. And against Zac the Attack Damage sap is close to worthless, because Unstable Matter deals a percentage of the target's MAXIMUM HEALTH as magic damage on a flat 5-second cooldown; it does not care what his AD is. That is also why armour is the wrong purchase here, which is exactly what _missing-interactions.json means by resistances-invalidated for this matchup. There is no slow in Unstable Matter either — the slow that pulls you off your zone is Stretching Strikes, 14 seconds at rank 1 at 800 range.
audit.corrected: Chomp: AD sap and a movement slow, and the AD sap buys little here. Unstable Matter (flat 5s): percent-max-health magic. Stretching Strikes (14s, 800 range) is the slow and the pull.

audit.whatIsWrong: The blob mechanic is described as something Zac does between trades — "regenerate blobs", "Regenerate passive blobs between trades", "if he drops a blob, step on it".
audit.why: Riot's text is more specific and more useful: Zac sheds a chunk each time he hits an enemy WITH AN ABILITY, and reabsorbs it to restore health. So the chunks appear during the trade, generated by his own casts, and denying them is an in-combat action rather than a between-trades one. Standing on the chunk while you keep biting is the play; walking over to it afterwards is not.
audit.corrected: Chunks drop whenever an ability of his lands, so deny them mid-trade, not between trades.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect confirmed: no cooldown number appears in either layer, and breakdown.cooldowns names Elastic Slingshot with no figure.
audit.why: Elastic Slingshot 21/18/15/12/9s, Stretching Strikes 14/12.5/11/9.5/8s, Unstable Matter a flat 5s, Let's Bounce! 120/105/90s, against Chomp's flat 3.5s, Pillar of Ice's 21s and Subjugate's 120s. Two pairs matter: Pillar of Ice and Elastic Slingshot are both 21 seconds at rank 1, so they trade exactly one for one early; and Subjugate and Let's Bounce! are both 120 at rank 1, so whoever spends first loses the second fight.
audit.corrected: Figures added to breakdown.cooldowns, phases[2], phases[4], report[5], dosFull[0], dontsFull[1], spikes[3], mid and three whys.

edits.before: At level 1, walk up and Chomp every time Zac steps in to last-hit — the flat damage plus the attack-speed steal immediately punishes his melee range, and if he drops a blob, step on it before he can recover it. He has no reliable level-1 damage to trade back with and his only sustain is the blobs, so denying them is as good as denying his health bar. At level 2, place Frozen Domain between yourself and the minion wave and trade inside it; his W slow cannot keep you out of your own ice and your healing continuously resets the damage he tries to stack. At level 3, the kit is complete — if he ever tries to fight back, Pillar cuts off his retreat and locks him in your domain while Chomp stacks the AD drain each hit.
edits.after: At level 1, walk up and Chomp every time Zac steps in to last-hit — the flat damage punishes his melee range, and every chunk his abilities shed is one you can stand on before he reabsorbs it. He has no reliable level-1 damage to trade back with and Cell Division is his only sustain, so denying the chunks is as good as denying his health bar. At level 2, place Frozen Domain between yourself and the wave and trade inside it; the slow that could drag you out is Stretching Strikes at 14s, not Unstable Matter. At level 3 the kit is complete on both sides — his Unstable Matter is a flat 5 seconds of percent-max-health magic, which the AD sap answers nothing about, while Pillar of Ice seals his retreat with terrain and a slow.

edits.before: The level 6 power spike here is extreme: Subjugate rips a percentage of Zac's current Armor and Magic Resistance and pastes it onto you, so the tankier he has been building, the more devastating the all-in. Cast R the instant he commits, drop Frozen Domain for the speed and healing, and use Chomp every cooldown to compound the AS debuff on top of the resistance drain — he physically cannot duel you in this window. His primary counterplay is Elastic Slingshot either away or into an angle where your Pillar is not ready; watch for the wind-up animation and place Pillar at his landing zone to knock him up and reset his disengage attempt. If he builds HP-stacking items like Heartsteel, that only inflates the value of Subjugate's percentage-drain further.
edits.after: The level 6 power spike here is extreme: Subjugate takes 40% of Zac's current armour and magic resist and pastes it onto you, plus a fifth of his maximum health as damage and the same again as healing, doubling over the next 4 seconds — so the tankier he has built, the more devastating the all-in. Cast it the instant he commits, drop Frozen Domain for the speed and the healing, and Chomp on every 3.5-second cooldown. His counterplay is Elastic Slingshot away, or into an angle your Pillar cannot cover: it is 21 seconds at rank 1, exactly your own Pillar of Ice, so watch for the wind-up and lay the terrain across the flight path rather than on the landing point. Heartsteel only inflates what Subjugate takes.

edits.before: In the late game this lane becomes conditional rather than free — Zac's role shifts to team-fight initiator and his Elastic Slingshot into a five-man pile is genuinely threatening regardless of the lane result. Your job is to stay close enough to Subjugate him the moment he lands so his CC chain is interrupted before his team collapses on the target. In a straight side-lane 1v1 you still win as long as R is available; without it, his CC and blob sustain can stall you out long enough for help to arrive. Iceborn Gauntlet and your accumulated resistances from previous Subjugate uses keep you relevant through team fights — dive their backline and burn R on whoever is tankiest.
edits.after: In the late game this lane becomes conditional rather than free — Zac's role shifts to team-fight initiator and Elastic Slingshot into a five-man pile is threatening regardless of the lane result. Stay close enough to Subjugate him the moment he lands, so the CC chain breaks before his team collapses on the target. Count his revive too: Cell Division splits him into four bloblets on fatal damage, each carrying a share of his max health, armour and MR, on a five-minute cooldown — the bloblets are the kill, and once it is spent you have five minutes against a mortal Zac. Without R up, his CC and chunk sustain stall you out.

notes: Mirror conflict to flag rather than resolve: audits/top/zac__trundle.json states that Zac's full layer "already reads Trundle/Skill/Zac/Zac/Trundle/Zac/Zac" and proposes moving Zac's content chart to match. On disk right now, both of Zac's layers and both of Trundle's read Trundle/Trundle/Trundle/Skill/Trundle/Trundle/Skill — all four agree, and that shape fits Trundle's 52.90%. I therefore made no chart edits; if the zac__trundle chart edits do land, the two directions will disagree and mirror-fix will have to pick. See questionsForUser. Substantively, the biggest fix here is the Pillar of Ice placement: three fields tell the player to drop it on the Slingshot's LANDING spot to knock Zac out of the air, and the pillar has no knock-up — it is terrain, so it belongs across the flight path. Also corrected throughout: 'AS steal' (Chomp saps AD, and against Unstable Matter's percent-max-health magic the AD sap barely matters), and 'his W slow' (Unstable Matter has no slow; the slow and the pull are Stretching Strikes).
